result.summary: Expands the `ipc` fuzz target to test bidirectional communication through client callbacks and validate server-side argument deserialization before values return over the pipe. It also sends arbitrary raw Cap'n Proto request and response payloads for `CTransaction` and `UniValue` to test error handling when deserializing malformed data directly in `libmultiprocess` clients and servers.
result.problem: The initial IPC fuzz target only tested round-trip calls where data was serialized by `libmultiprocess` before being deserialized, meaning corrupted or malformed payloads were not tested against client/server deserializers, reverse callback channels were unexercised, and serialization errors on the client-to-server path could be masked during the return trip.
evidence: Addresses reviewer feedback from #35118 suggesting server-side assertions on incoming arguments to detect one-way serialization mismatches.
Follows up on multiprocess fuzzing roadmap in #23015 by testing raw input deserialization and bidirectional callback support.
result.scope_notes: Touches only IPC fuzz target harness files (`src/ipc/test/fuzz/`).
result.changed_since_previous: No structural changes; the PR was rebased with minor touch-ups to the fuzz harness.
result.card: Expands the IPC fuzz target to test bidirectional callback communication, server-side argument integrity, and client/server deserialization of arbitrary raw transaction and UniValue payloads. The change ensures libmultiprocess and Cap'n Proto serialization hooks handle malformed inputs gracefully without relying solely on valid round-trip serialization. It builds on #35118 and contributes toward multiprocess fuzzing goals in #23015.

risk.why: Touches only fuzz testing code; a bug would cause false fuzz test failures or unhandled exceptions during fuzzing without impacting node binaries.
